title: Cultivation No-Dig
site: Reconstructed starter bed over grass at the left edge of the allotment's central grass path when facing John's pale green shed. John works from the adjacent path.

joint_render.prompt:
Create the three finished editorial photographs for John Lennon's UK vegetable growing book “Starting a No-Dig Bed”. Deliver ONE very wide, horizontal triptych, exactly three equally wide SQUARE photographs in a single row edge-to-edge, target 3:1 canvas. No margins, type, caption, collage within a panel, labels, or borders. These are three documentary shots of the same one-metre-wide, roughly two-metre-long starter bed in the SAME spring afternoon session. Each will be cropped out and printed separately at 45 mm wide. Get the action plainly visible at that size. Show the same real John and exact same modest location, person scale, bed size and camera position in every shot. Three distinct instants, easy to understand across the row.

Use attached image 1 (A02) for the ground plan ONLY, not the aerial camera angle. John's plot is on the LEFT of the main mown grass path as one looks towards HIS pale mint-green timber shed. The bed is wholly inside the plot left of the path. His plot ends just beyond the pale green shed. Image 2 (A11) gives the actual ground-level Cornish allotment, materials, shiplap shed, hedges, John's body/outfit. Image 3 is John's real face: high forehead, slight smile lines and short greying beard curving into a soft rounded chin, no angular jutting jaw or exaggerated beard. His build and age as photographed. Olive knit cap, teal blue fleece jacket with NO microphone or logo, blue jeans and work boots from A11 in ALL THREE frames. Image 4 (H16-18) gives the exact cardboard, surface texture and compost finish from John's real earlier no-dig bed, USE AS A MATERIAL REFERENCE ONLY. The setting for the finished photos is exclusively the allotment, outdoors. Give the small new bed sloping unboarded edges.

Composition in EACH square: same documentary camera standing along the grass path slightly forward of John, aimed down obliquely at the long bed so hands and material read clearly. Foreground dominated by the bed. Leave a narrow uninterrupted strip of the existing mown grass path on the right, from foreground to rear; far corner, grass margin and same sliver of pale green shed at top left should register in exactly the same place in all panels. Bed extends leftwards into John's plot. A hint of hedge and adjacent cultivated ground, few sky/background distractions. No neighbouring brown shed, no greenhouse, no house garden, no raised timber frame. Imagine this bed footprint at its beginning with grass and low ordinary weeds growing there. Realistic boots, hands, knees and tools bearing weight. John works comfortably from the path on the right in all three; no stepping on this bed.

LEFT: Cover the ground. John kneels and is actually laying a last broad piece of plain brown flattened corrugated cardboard overlapping the next one by a handspan or more. Bare hands pressing the overlap, little creases and torn box edges. Several sheets lie flat directly on low green grass, a small strip of still-uncovered grass inside the far end for context. No logos, printing, tape, staples or compost. The same bordering right-hand path is entirely clear.
MIDDLE: Add the compost. John comfortably draws the BACK of a short-handled sturdy straight garden rake over mature, dark brown, crumbly compost to level and gently firm it. Relaxed stance on path, hands correctly gripping the straight handle, rake head symmetrical and centrally attached, actually touching the compost. Most cardboard now has about four inches/10 cm of compost across it, with a little cardboard still clearly visible in the last unfinished corner. A genuine, low sloping compost lip where light falls on its edge. Realistically heterogeneous organic crumb; no manure chunks or huge heaps. Grass aisle remains clear. Keep same body scale and outdoor light.
RIGHT: Start growing. The SAME entire bed now finished in dark friable level compost, slopes naturally down at the boundaries, all cardboard covered. John kneels on the path and uses a hand trowel with one hand while easing a modest young loose-leaf lettuce plug into a small planting hole with the other. A few small well-spaced lettuce transplants behind it, at most 5-6, leaving plenty of bare compost visible around them. Real small plants and believable light roots/soil. Show actual handling of the transplant, no spade, no random tools or extra hands. The exact same grass aisle is still visible. Natural soft Cornish spring daylight, honest colours and texture, garden magazine documentary photography, no filters, no illustration, neutral exposure, anatomically convincing, candid and quietly practical.
